conviction_note: The print turns on one thing the market cannot yet see: how management sizes the 26 Oct customer ramp-down against its 40%+ FY guide (needs Q4 near $85M) and the large programs it said it would add once won. The stock is already -38.5% over 20 sessions and was -12.5% intraday today with no new cause found, short interest is ~13% of shares outstanding, and this name has sold its last three reaffirmations or beats. The two measurements roughly cancel: the findings sum to +0.7, p_up 51 on a 20% absolute move gives +0.4. The direction is a coin flip; the size is not.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $84.7M (Zacks preview, https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2862396/ via search; Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/INOD/earnings-forecasts also $84.7M; a third source quoted $83.3M). The company's own guide of 40%+ growth on FY2025 revenue of $251.7M (https://investor.innodata.com/news/news-details/2026/Innodata-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) less H1 2026 revenue of $182.2M (Q1 $90.1M, Q2 $92.1M) implies H2 >= $170.2M, about $85.1M a quarter, so the revenue bar sits at the guide floor. The EPS bar is disputed ($0.17 / $0.21 Zacks / $0.26 Benzinga), so EPS findings are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,521,023 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 13.15% of shares outstanding (~14.6% of a ~31M float), 3.65 days to cover, down 3.1% from 4,663,829 on 2026-09-30 (https://altindex.com/ticker/inod/short-interest). findings.finding: On 26 Oct 2026 Innodata reportedly let go of nearly 550 staff in India, about 5% of its 10,107 year-end headcount, plus an uncounted number of raters, QA, team leads and managers in the Philippines. The termination emails cite a 'ramp-down of the business assignment'. The company has not commented. Its two largest customers were 71% of Q2 revenue (37% and 34%). The release is management's first chance to say whether this touches the 40%+ FY guide, which needs Q4 near $85M, and the cut most plausibly lands in Q4, since Q3 closed on 30 Sep. Netted against it: in August management said large potential programs from new and existing customers were excluded from the guide, that it expected most to be won, and that it would add them once scope was final. A CEO change on 30 Sep (Singhal in, Abuhoff to executive chairman) makes this the new CEO's first guide, which raises the odds of a reset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this name trades on. The May 2026 raise from 35%+ to 40%+ with a ~$51M Big Tech program went +86.0%. The Feb 2026 first guide of 35%+ went -7.17%. The June 2026 standalone reaffirmation went -6.85%. The Aug 2026 reaffirmation with a 7% revenue beat went -4.81%. Reaffirmations have been sold; raises have been bought hard.
findings.why_not_priced: The fact itself is fully priced as a headline: -25% on 27 Oct and a further -16% since. What is not priced is its size. Taken pro rata, 550 of 10,107 staff is roughly 5% of revenue, about $4-5M a quarter. The ~$1.4bn to ~$1.3bn market cap has lost about $700M since 26 Oct, which prices something closer to losing the whole of one large customer. If the market had a number, the straddle would not be at 303% IV with a 46% spread, and the stock would not have fallen 12.5% today on no identified news.
findings.independence: HRKatha (https://www.hrkatha.com/news/layoff/innodata-layoffs-hit-india-and-the-philippines/, 2026-10-28) separately reports the Philippines cuts tied to 'declining service volumes from a major client project'. Both ultimately rest on India Today's reading of the termination email. The offsetting side, unbooked large programs, comes from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000903651/000110465926092010/tm2621499d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-08-06). Concentration and the CEO change come from the same release.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows advances from customers 'for unfulfilled obligations' of $67.0M at 30 Jun 2026, against $1.8M at 31 Dec 2025, plus $61.8M of incurred but unpaid project costs. A customer prepaid about three quarters of a quarter's revenue for work not yet delivered at the start of Q3. This underpins the Q3 revenue bar of $84.7M, which sits about 8% below Q2's $92.1M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been paid for lately. Q2 2026 beat by about 7% and the stock went -4.81%. Q1 2026 beat by a wide margin with a raise and went +86%, but that move was the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The figure sits in the 10-Q notes, not in the press release. In the Q2 call it was only called 'customer prepayments, which are a pass-through'. The previews quote consensus and the layoffs, not the advance balance. If the market read the advance as funded Q3 to Q4 work, a Q3 at or above $85M would not be in question, and today's selling into the print suggests it is. Caveat that sizes this down: pass-through revenue is low-margin, and some of the advance may already have been earned in Q3, which consensus partly reflects. Management also said in August that a sequential decline was 'certainly possible'.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript, CFO Chauhan on 'customer prepayments, which are a pass-through' and Abuhoff saying a Q3/Q4 sequential decline is 'certainly possible' (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2942769). Same company and same period, so this is partly the same document set.

findings.finding: Q2 adjusted gross margin was 49%, 9 points above the company's public 40% target, driven by mix toward higher-margin programs. Q2 EPS was $0.41 against a $0.21-0.25 consensus. The Q3 EPS bar ($0.17 / $0.21 / $0.26 across sources) assumes margin falls back. A margin-led EPS beat is likely even on flat-to-down revenue, but management warned that margin 'will depend on product mix' quarter to quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have been sold: Q2 2026 nearly doubled consensus EPS and the stock went -4.81%. In Q1 2025 the company beat and the stock went -15.79% on a revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The three EPS consensus figures disagree by 50%, so no single bar is anchored. Capped small because the bar is disputed and because this name sells its EPS beats.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K exhibit 99.1, adjusted EBITDA of $25.4M at 27.5% of revenue (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000903651/000110465926092010/tm2621499d1_ex99-1.htm). Same company and same quarter.

findings.finding: A $300M at-the-market equity program (Goldman lead, plus Craig-Hallum, Wells Fargo, Maxim and Wedbush) was filed on 6 Aug 2026, priced off $70.21. The Q3 10-Q, normally filed with the print, will show whether shares were sold. On use of proceeds, the prospectus says only general corporate purposes, with $250M of cash on hand (about $134M net of customer prepayments) and an undrawn $50M revolver. No corroborated use was found, so this is a mild negative. The Vanguard 13G/A at 30 Sep (1,712,403 shares = 4.98%) implies about 34.4M shares, unchanged from 31 Jul, which suggests little or no ATM use through Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None found for this name; the ATM itself was announced alongside the Q2 print, which went -4.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: The program is public. The new information would be usage or any Q4 issuance near $37, which nobody can see until the 10-Q. If the market feared dilution, it would show in borrow cost, which was not found.
findings.independence: Vanguard Schedule 13G/A, 2026-10-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/903651/000210011926001620/primary_doc.xml), implies share count was flat through 30 Sep.

findings.finding: Positioning: about 13.15% of shares outstanding short (4.52M shares, 3.65 days to cover, 15 Oct settlement, before the layoff report). Put/call open interest is 0.21. The stock is -38.5% over 20 sessions, -18.5% over 5, and 9% above its 52-week low going into the print. Any line the release clears (Q3 at or above $85M, FY guide held, a program added) meets a short base that has not covered and a long base that has already sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From similar positioning into the Q1 2026 print, the stock went +86% on a raise. With short interest of about 8-10%, it went -4.8% to -6.9% on reaffirmations.
findings.why_not_priced: The short count is public and stale. It predates the 26 Oct crash, so whether shorts pressed or covered since is unknown. Sized small because 13% is below the 18-23% levels at which this stage has seen squeezes, and an unexplained drawdown by itself is not evidence.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run-up figures) and the stockanalysis.com intraday quote of 2026-11-05 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/inod/). Independent of the short data.

findings.finding: Securities law firms opened investigations after the layoff report: Levi & Korsinsky (28 Oct), SueWallSt (~28 Oct) and SBS Law (~2 Nov). Each asks whether investors were told of the risk of the business reduction. That pressures management to quantify the ramp-down in the release or the 10-Q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Feb 2024 Wolfpack short report, a wave of law-firm notices followed and the stock recovered over subsequent prints. No measured print reaction to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: These are routine law-firm advertisements; they are fully public and close to irrelevant. Filed because the core requires every sourced fact to be filed, and sized at nearly zero.
findings.independence: stockanalysis.com news list showing SBS Law around 2 Nov (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/inod/).

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Appen's Q3 FY26 report (29 Oct, after Innodata last spoke) shows Appen Global revenue of $27.9M, +17% quarter on quarter, and two US frontier AI model builders added as customers, one a large former customer. US frontier-lab spending on data vendors was rising in Q3, the quarter Innodata reports. The share shift it shows cuts both ways.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of Innodata reacting to Appen prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an ASX filing from an Australian peer that US coverage of Innodata does not cite. It is only a proxy: different customers, and Appen's growth could come at a vendor's expense, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Appen H1 FY26 (2026-08-27) showed Global revenue -26.9%, so Q3 is a turn for Appen rather than a trend.

baseline_tension: No skew number is available. The run-up (-38.5% over 20 days, -18.5% over 5) and today's -12.5% say the market expects a guide cut. The layoff evidence agrees on direction but appears small against the drawdown, so the findings net to almost nothing and p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (net of the rest): guidance/layoff finding resized from -1.5 to -1.0, netted against the unbooked large programs management said it would add to guidance once won.
